meta.case_name: Government Agriculture Operations (Level of Difficulty case)

prompt.context: The federal government of a country is investigating whether to restart a rubber factory in the western part of the country. The factory was operational in the past but has not been used for 7 years. The plant was closed due to terrorism in the area, which has now come down significantly though there are still issues and skirmishes reported. If rejuvenated, the plant may become a target for rebels. All the equipment is considered useable, but the government still estimates spending $12M to rejuvenate the plant, which would enable it to produce up to 10M lbs of rubber per month. The demand for rubber worldwide is strong, but rubber must be transported to an export port via trains; up to 2 trains per day can be used for this purpose.
prompt.question: Should the government restart the rubber factory? Assess the financial return on investment and other relevant considerations.

clarifying_info.q: What are the raw materials needed?
clarifying_info.a: The plant needs gum resin. 3 lbs of resin after processing results in 1 lb of rubber.

clarifying_info.q: Where does the resin come from?
clarifying_info.a: Resin must be transported from the capital. Up to 4 trains per day can be used for incoming resin transport.

clarifying_info.q: What price can rubber be sold at?
clarifying_info.a: Rubber sells at $20 per lb. Gum resin costs $5 per lb.
The rubber would be sold in the commodity market to buyers worldwide.

clarifying_info.q: What is the demand for rubber in the market?
clarifying_info.a: Market demand is strong. For this analysis, assume whatever the plant produces can be sold.

framework: Analyze financial benefits of the investment: ROI, production capacity, and value chain (Raw Material Supplier → Manufacturing Plant → Customers)
Identify constraints: equipment capacity is 10M lbs/month but supply and distribution may be the binding constraint — map the full value chain to surface transportation bottlenecks
Quantify other government-specific benefits: employment and economic development
Identify and assess risks: terrorism, price volatility, labor, single supplier, sole transportation mode
Develop recommendation with key numbers, risks, and next steps

questions.prompt: Calculate monthly production capacity — how much rubber can actually be produced and shipped?
questions.guidance: Candidate must work through both the outgoing (rubber export) and incoming (resin supply) train capacity, then identify which is the binding constraint. Do NOT assume 10M lbs/month; the answer is lower. Perform all calculations on a monthly basis (25 working days).

math.setup: Outgoing train capacity determines how much rubber can be exported. Incoming train capacity determines how much resin can be supplied. The 3:1 resin-to-rubber ratio converts resin supply into rubber output. The bottleneck is whichever is smaller.
steps: Outgoing train daily capacity: 2 trains × 8 bogies/train × 25 cases/bogie × 500 lbs/case = 200,000 lbs/day
Outgoing monthly capacity: 200,000 × 25 days = 5,000,000 lbs of rubber/month
Incoming train daily capacity: 4 trains × 10 bogies/train × 25 barrels/bogie × 640 lbs/barrel = 640,000 lbs of resin/day
Incoming monthly resin: 640,000 × 25 = 16,000,000 lbs of resin/month
Convert resin to rubber: 16,000,000 ÷ 3 = 5,333,333 lbs of rubber/month
Bottleneck: outgoing train capacity at 5,000,000 lbs/month is the binding constraint
math.answer: Monthly rubber production is 5,000,000 lbs, constrained by outgoing train capacity (not equipment capacity of 10M lbs or incoming resin supply of ~5.33M rubber-equivalent lbs).

questions.prompt: Build the monthly income statement and calculate ROI on the $12M investment.
questions.guidance: Candidate should build a clean P&L using 5M lbs output. Key insight: margins are very thin at ~1%. ROI is approximately 1 year ($1M profit/month vs. $12M investment). NPV analysis is not required.

math.setup: Use 5M lbs/month production. Revenue = price × volume. Material cost = resin cost × resin volume needed (3 lbs resin per 1 lb rubber). Transportation cost covers all trains both inbound and outbound, all 25 days.
steps: Transportation cost: $40,000/trip × (4 inbound + 2 outbound) trains/day × 25 days = $6M/month
math.answer: Monthly profit = $1M; payback period = 12 months; net margin = 1% (wafer thin).

questions.prompt: What other areas would you explore to support a recommendation to the government?
questions.guidance: Candidate should highlight government-specific benefits beyond pure financials, then enumerate risks with mitigations.

brainstorming.prompt: What are the key risks and benefits beyond the financial return that the government should weigh?

categories.name: Government/Social Benefits
ideas: Employment: $8M/month labor cost signals a highly labor-intensive operation creating significant local jobs
Economic development of an underdeveloped or conflict-affected region
Potential multiplier effect on surrounding local economy

categories.name: Financial/Market Risks
ideas: Very low margin (1%) — highly exposed to price fluctuations in resin and rubber
Mitigation: forward contracts on resin purchases (lock in input costs)
Mitigation: forward contracts on rubber sales (lock in revenue)
Capacity upside if transport bottleneck resolved — could double profit if outgoing trains increased

categories.name: Labor Risks
ideas: Difficulty attracting and retaining workers in a conflict zone
Mitigation: introduce automation to reduce labor dependency
Mitigation: facilitate migration of labor from other regions

categories.name: Terrorism Risk
ideas: Plant could become a rebel target once operational
Mitigation: involve community leaders in the process
Mitigation: arrange government or private security for the plant

categories.name: Supply Chain Risks
ideas: Sole dependency on trains for both inbound resin and outbound rubber
Mitigation: maintain adequate safety stock of resin and rubber
Mitigation: ensure rail tracks are protected in sensitive areas
Mitigation: diversify into other transportation modes — invest in roads or waterways
Single supplier for resin — concentration risk

recommendation: Go ahead with the investment — the plant is financially viable, returning $1M/month profit and recovering the $12M investment in approximately 1 year
Production is limited to 5M lbs/month by outgoing train capacity, not by equipment; addressing this bottleneck could significantly increase profits going forward
risks: Margins are extremely thin at 1%, making the business highly sensitive to input (resin) or output (rubber) price changes
Terrorism risk remains — the plant could become a target, disrupting operations
Single supplier and sole reliance on rail create fragile supply chain
Labor availability in a conflict-affected area is uncertain
next_steps: Assess how the plant can be staffed and whether labor can be sourced or migrated to the region
Evaluate feasibility of increasing outgoing train capacity to relieve the production bottleneck
Conduct a detailed terrorism threat assessment and develop a security and community engagement plan
Explore diversifying resin suppliers and alternative transportation modes to reduce supply chain concentration risk
